storylines.label: Claude Fable
storylines.latest_title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)

prior_narrative.tldr: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5 as long-horizon models "made safe for general use," but a US export-control directive citing national security suspended access days later — critics argued the controls themselves weakened US cyber defense. The models returned gated on Amazon Bedrock behind a data-sharing opt-in, then redeployed from July 1 once the controls lifted, backed by updated cybersecurity safeguards.
prior_narrative.whats_new: Anthropic published details on Fable 5's cyber safeguards — what its classifiers do and don't block — plus a first-draft jailbreak severity framework, two days into the post-suspension redeploy.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: The classifier scope and jailbreak severity framework are the concrete terms of "made safe for general use" — the thing platform engineers need to evaluate before trusting Fable 5 in security-sensitive flows, and the direct response to the critique that the export controls themselves weakened US cyber defense.

status.detail: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 launched "made safe for general use," were suspended by a US export-control directive, returned on Amazon Bedrock only under a data-sharing opt-in, redeployed from July 1 after the controls were lifted, and on July 2 Anthropic detailed the cyber classifiers and jailbreak severity framework behind that redeploy.

beats.headline: Claude Fable 5 + Mythos 5 ship — "made safe for general use"
beats.summary: Anthropic ships the Mythos-class Fable 5 and the unguarded Mythos 5, billed as made safe for general use.

beats.headline: US export-control directive suspends access
beats.summary: Citing national security, the US government orders access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 suspended days after launch.

beats.headline: Critics say the controls themselves harm US cyber defense
beats.summary: Commentary argues the export controls weakened US cyber defense, pointing to the underlying jailbreak that triggered the suspension.

beats.headline: Back on Bedrock — but only with data-sharing opted in
beats.summary: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 return on Amazon Bedrock gated behind provider_data_share: prompts and outputs go to Anthropic for 30-day retention with human review.

beats.headline: Export controls lifted — redeploying July 1 with new safeguards
beats.summary: With the export directive lifted, Anthropic redeploys Fable 5 from July 1, adding updated cybersecurity safeguards and a new industry jailbreak framework.

beats.headline: Anthropic details what the cyber classifiers block
beats.summary: Two days into redeploy, Anthropic publishes what is and isn't blocked by Fable 5's cyber classifiers, plus a first draft of an industry jailbreak severity framework.

open_questions: Does the July 1 redeployment restore standard private-inference terms, or does the Bedrock provider_data_share requirement persist?
Do the published cyber classifiers close the specific jailbreak that triggered the export-control suspension, or does exposure remain?
Will other frontier labs adopt the first-draft jailbreak severity framework, or does it stay Anthropic-only?
Is Fable 5 / Mythos 5 redeploying beyond Bedrock — first-party API or other clouds — on private-inference terms?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: Read Anthropic's classifier scope and jailbreak severity framework before trusting Fable 5 in security-sensitive flows, confirm whether Bedrock still forces provider_data_share (30-day retention, human review), and keep a fallback model wired so a single-flagship dependency can't strand you again.
